prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle

statement.case_for: I keep B001 as my preferred configuration after the full first-round exchange. The reason is the one I gave at the start and I have not seen it answered: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a compact, analytically transparent calculation that gives a specific, falsifiable number, the magic angle near 1.1 degrees, where the Dirac velocity vanishes and the bands flatten. Seven years later an experiment at that angle found correlated insulators and superconductivity. That is a prediction that was tested, and the mechanism that makes the bands flat is understood. This is different from the situation where only the phenomenon is known. The result has also been reproduced in many laboratories and carried over to other moire platforms with tunable correlated and topological states, so the claim does not rest on one device or one group. I now phrase the citation more narrowly than in round 1, around the magic-angle flat bands and the observed correlated phases, so that it does not claim all twisted-bilayer theory or the open pairing question. I should be candid about the committee picture: six colleagues prefer B007 and every B001 reservation I hold is also held by Eriksson. I keep B001 because on the criterion of a tested, understood mechanism it is stronger, not because I discount the clock.
statement.case_against: The case against B001 is stronger than I suggested in round 1. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved, device-to-device variation from twist-angle disorder is real, and the field is about eight years old. Several colleagues, Olsson most pointedly, say the prize would be stronger in a few years, and I cannot show that this is wrong. The credit problem is also real and cannot be removed by wording: Cao and the first experimental authors, other groups and the crystal growers, and the earlier twisted-bilayer flat-band work of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto all fall outside three names. I am relying on memory for that priority history, as are several others on B007. If a record check shows that the earlier work is closer to the origin of the magic-angle result than I believe, my own criterion about who first identified the mechanism would count against the three-name configuration and I would move to B007. By contrast B007 has two clean names, a settled experimental claim and, by the chair's account, broad support.

responses.point: Eva moved B007 ahead of twisted bilayer graphene because the experimental claim is settled while the pairing mechanism is not, asks for the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto record to be examined under the original-work criterion, and says B001 would be a strong prize a few years from now and no weaker for waiting.
responses.response: I accept the substance of her priority point and agree the record should be checked before the committee commits. Where I differ is on the pairing mechanism. The question for the prize is what was discovered, and the existence of correlated insulators and superconductivity at the predicted angle is as well established as the clock's 1e-18 uncertainty; what is open is the explanation of one phase, and an open mechanism does not by itself make a discovery premature. I do grant that waiting costs B001 little and that a premature prize costs more than a late one, which is the best argument for B007 this year and B001 later. My answer is that the case for B001 will not be much stronger after waiting unless the credit history is clarified, and that can be done now. I also do not believe the earlier flat-band work gives a quantitative magic angle; I flag that as memory and not as checked fact.

responses.point: Ulf, as Secretary, calls B007 the candidate hardest to argue against, with a clean two-person attribution and a redefinition of the second as a concrete maturity measure, and he ranks B001 second as quite mature for its age but slightly early.
responses.response: I agree on attribution and I take the redefinition of the second as a fair maturity argument for the clock, although he and Kroll both note that it has not happened and so part of the impact is prospective, while the moire result has already been reproduced and extended. His questions on the chair's list on B001 deserve a straight answer, so: if only two names were possible I would keep MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero. Bistritzer co-authored the 2011 calculation, but a two-name prize is the one place where the three-name limit forces a choice between the theory and the experiment, and a citation that names the prediction and the experiment is more defensible than one that names a single calculation twice. I accept that the choice between them is a judgement call and Ulf's own two-name idea reflects the same difficulty. The citation should name the 2011 prediction and the 2018 observation as separate steps.

responses.point: Stefan describes the lattice clock as a new measurement capability, notes it is reproduced and compared at JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST and SYRTE and used for redshift, constants and dark matter, and asks whether a prize before the redefinition of the second is timely or slightly early.
responses.response: I think his reproduction and use arguments are correct and they are the strongest part of the B007 case; I do not dispute them. On timing I would say that waiting for the redefinition is a question of timing and not of maturity, and that the same logic would let the committee hold B001 until the pairing mechanism is settled, which I do not accept. Consistency matters here: if we treat the pending redefinition as irrelevant to the clock's scientific standing, we should treat the open pairing mechanism the same way for B001. I also note his disclosed link to the Hall laboratory, which he says he will raise with the chair; I see no reason to exclude him, but the committee should record that decision on B007 explicitly, as it bears on the largest bloc of support.

responses.point: Goran concedes that his own first choice B058 reflected his neighbourhood, argues that the magic-wavelength condition is a simple general mechanism like the Bistritzer-MacDonald model, and asks me to say whether the open superconductivity and the credit to Cao make me prefer waiting a few years.
responses.response: I agree that the magic-wavelength condition is a clean mechanism and that it matches what I look for in a model; the analogy is fair, and it is why B007 is my first alternative and not a distant one. Answering his question directly: the open superconductivity does not lead me to prefer waiting, but the credit to Cao and earlier theory is a real reason for caution, and if the record check turns up a stronger claim for others than the three names reflect, I would prefer B007 now over a contested B001. My difference with him is that the clock is metrology that tests the world with a better instrument, while the moire result shows a new class of correlated matter; both are legitimate prizes, and I would not call the clock an instrument only. I am not arguing that his judgement is biased by being an experimentalist.

responses.point: Olle agrees on B001, puts the credit weakness on Cao and the first experimental authors and earlier twisted-bilayer theory, and finds the Bistritzer-MacDonald contribution defensible as the specific quantitative magic-angle prediction.
responses.response: We are close, and I take his point that the citation should be worded around the magic-angle flat bands so as not to claim all twisted-bilayer theory; I have changed my wording accordingly. I would push on one point where we are still too comfortable: we both say the credit is defensible, but neither of us has checked the early papers. If the committee is to rely on B001 it should ask an expert to establish what Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto actually computed in 2007 and how it relates to the 2011 magic-angle condition, and what the 2018 experimental authors contributed beyond the credited names. Until then we should be honest that the two B001 supporters are as dependent on recollection as the B007 supporters are.

uncertainties: Whether the early twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) changes the credit for the magic-angle prediction; this is from memory and can be settled by an expert report.
Whether Cao and the first experimental authors, and the groups who reproduced the correlated phases, can be left out of a three-name prize without making the award look unfair.
Whether the open pairing mechanism will be read as a maturity problem by the six members who prefer B007, and whether the committee treats the unredefined second the same way.

Whether the committee judges the lattice clock to be distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes; if it does, B007 is the safer configuration and I would regard it as an acceptable outcome.
I cannot say with confidence that the field has matured enough: the strongest argument against my position is Olsson's, that a prize in a few years loses nothing.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent. I have no collaboration with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori or Ye, or with any other candidate on the shortlist. I am in the Gothenburg physics environment that is closely linked to Chalmers, where Johansson and Olsson work, but I have no specific collaboration with them and see no reason to recuse on B001 or B007. I note that I have not been given any reason to change this disclosure since round 1.
